answer.answer: Prioritize `/in/playerActivity`: keep stale data available and refresh it asynchronously under a lock so foreground requests never perform the expensive rebuild. Separately, make `/p/:identifier/raids` render shell plus local raid results before Bungie collectible enrichment, and defer Pantheon until its tab is selected or share its collectible fetch. The evidence is a historical 2026-06-12 snapshot; these changes and their results remain proposals pending implementation and new telemetry.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. Over 7 days it recorded 13,210 RUM calls with 3.69 s average and 12.03 s p95 latency; exact `GET /in/playerActivity` APM recorded 23,255 spans with 1.99 s average and 13.03 s p95. It also sits in the high-traffic analytics-home fan-out, while foreground rebuild logs showed shard scans and math taking roughly 18 s and 16 s at p95.

Implement stale-while-revalidate for player activity: retain a longer-lived stale value, refresh it every five minutes in the background, and protect refresh with a single-flight or distributed lock. The code currently reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache and falls back to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`, making a web request pay for the Redis shard scan when the five-minute cache expires or is absent; Discord already treats a missing cache as no-data instead of rebuilding synchronously. Define explicit fresh/stale TTLs and continue serving stale data when refresh fails.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie `ProfileWCollectibles`, not local raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for all sources, including `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)`, while raid-difficulty summaries were about 2.7 ms, carries about 6.1 ms average, and seals about 0.6 ms. The route also starts a separate Pantheon `ProfileWCollectibles` fetch before that tab is opened. answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer. The correction moves the product boundary beyond learned memory or retrieval: it must preserve resumable work state and prove that a fresh agent can correctly continue and advance real work, with Obsidian serving only as a prototype corpus and human-readable projection.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer for agents. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, transcript archive, synchronized folder, retrieval product, or memory database; its purpose is durable machine continuity across agent ecosystems and trust domains.

Beyond durable knowledge and learned patterns, Straylight must preserve the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next actions. A later agent must be able to inspect how that state was reached, revise it as evidence changes, verify it, and leave a better durable state behind.

Obsidian and Markdown are not the product boundary because Straylight is agent-first, while human-readable notes are prototype inputs, projections, and export formats. The Obsidian vault supplies an excellent representative corpus, and Metis organizes that human knowledge base, but raw Markdown is neither assumed to be the canonical storage representation nor the canonical interaction model; full sources and artifacts remain authoritative while summaries, embeddings, indexes, and context packs are derived aids.

The first benchmark was too narrow because it was retrieval-readiness work over 44 non-private notes, 20 questions, and 53 gold evidence items, exercising memory.open, memory.query, and memory.read while leaving model-directed memory.compute and memory.verify untested. Retrieval-only scores are now a regression lane, not the product gate. The expanded evaluation must prove that a fresh agent can resume, iterate, compute, verify, and advance representative real workloads—Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning under changing constraints, and Straylight’s own evolution—while maintaining final-answer correctness, completeness, source fidelity, temporal and contradiction handling, and correct durable checkpoints, revisions, handoffs, and next-state artifacts. It must compare direct filesystem tools, a model-directed agent workspace, and fixed handoff/context packs.
